corpus_meta.name: GetHired Cybersecurity Fresher Corpus
corpus_meta.scope: Entry-level / 0-1 years experience cybersecurity roles only (India-focused)
roles_explicitly_excluded: SOC L2/L3, Senior, or Lead roles of any kind
corpus_meta.sample_size_note: This pass pulled skill-tag data from roughly 120+ distinct postings surfaced across ~19 targeted searches (Glassdoor India, Indeed India/US, Naukri-aggregator reports) covering Chennai, Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Kerala, Hyderabad, and general India/US listings. Weights below are counted from how often each skill appeared across those listings' structured 'Skills:' tags and description text, not from a full raw scrape. This is a meaningfully larger and more systematic sample than v0.1, but is still search-engine-mediated (snippets + aggregator pages), not a deduplicated database.
corpus_meta.known_limitation: For statistically rigorous, continuously-refreshed accuracy at true scale, this should be replaced by the planned GitHub Action job that queries a job-postings API (e.g. Adzuna) directly and computes frequency from full posting text on a schedule. This file is a strong seed corpus, not a substitute for that pipeline.
sources: Glassdoor India (city-filtered: Chennai, Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Kerala, Hyderabad, India-wide)
Naukri (via aggregator report citing 229 live fresher postings)
Company-adjacent postings (Wipro, TCS, Deloitte, IBM via career/job-board mirrors)
corpus_meta.role_weighting_note: v0.3.0 split each item's single flat weight into per-role weights (soc_analyst / vapt / network_security_engineer / generalist) reflecting how central that item actually is to each specific track, not one blended number. Grounded in a researcher pass over SOC/VAPT/NetSec entry-level posting patterns, the NICE Workforce Framework's Cyber Defense Analyst / Vulnerability Assessment / Network Services work roles, and cert bodies' own positioning (CompTIA's Security+ -> CySA+ vs Network+ -> CCNA progressions, eJPT vs OSCP entry-level framing). generalist approximates the old flat weight; it is not a simple average of the other three.

certifications.count_basis: Consistently named as the single most-requested baseline cert in fresher-specific SOC/analyst postings; explicit requirement in ~41% of postings that mention it. CompTIA positions it as the foundational gateway cert across SOC, junior security engineer, and general entry roles alike.

Top single most-requested cert across 229 aggregated India fresher networking+security postings, but entry Network Security Engineer postings specifically lean on it far more heavily than SOC or VAPT postings, which mention it only as a nice-to-have.
CompTIA's own certification progression ties CySA+ to threat-detection/defensive-analyst roles (Security+ -> CySA+), making it notably more SOC-specific than a generic entry cert.
Positioned industry-wide as the absolute-entry cert for career-changers/interns with no prior specialization, so it's least track-differentiated and most relevant to the broad Generalist track.
Repeatedly described in pentest-track sources as the realistic first entry-level pentesting cert, more genuinely fresher-aligned than OSCP.

Community consensus frames OSCP as the gold standard for red-team/advanced pentest work — aspirational rather than a true 0-yr entry-level requirement; eJPT is the truer entry VAPT cert. Rare at true 0-yr level; appears as 'preferred' not 'required' in this sample

tools.count_basis: Appeared across nearly every SOC Analyst / SOC L1 fresher posting in this sample; essentially absent from VAPT and Network Security Engineer entry postings.
Network Security Engineer postings put firewall/router configuration as the primary technical skill; SOC uses IDS/IPS mainly as an alert source rather than something they configure.
Genuinely cross-cutting rather than VAPT-exclusive — used for vulnerability scanning in VAPT engagements, network hardening in NetSec, and vuln-alert context in SOC.
Packet analysis is described as a core diagnostic skill specifically for Network Security Engineer postings; supporting tool elsewhere.

Cross-cutting, not a single-track specialty — SOC monitors/audits AD activity, VAPT tests AD as attack surface, NetSec administers/hardens it as infrastructure. Deliberately not MINOR for any of the three.

concepts_frameworks.count_basis: The single most frequently tagged skill in this entire sample across all fresher role types; the primary differentiator for Network Security Engineer postings specifically.
Extremely common generic tag across nearly all postings sampled — undifferentiated by track.
Maps directly onto NICE's Cyber Defense Analyst work role; VAPT touches it only via reporting handoff.
Maps directly onto NICE's distinct Vulnerability Assessment and Management specialty area, which lines up most closely with the VAPT track.
Repeatedly named as the essential SOC L1 skill in guides on the role; VAPT/NetSec use logs diagnostically but it isn't their primary function.

Cross-cutting like Active Directory — VAPT sources note Windows registry/services/AD knowledge is needed for Windows-target engagements, so it isn't SOC-exclusive. Tagged nearly as often as Linux across this sample — freshers expected to know both OS families
VAPT sources specifically emphasize 'strong networking + Linux fundamentals' as the ideal-candidate profile.

Governance-flavored, appears more in SOC/NetSec postings tied to compliance auditing than in hands-on VAPT roles. Appeared more often than expected even in fresher postings — usually as 'exposure to' rather than 'implements'
Fundamental awareness-level, not strongly differentiated by track.
Least emphasized at true entry-level across all postings found; slightly more present in Network Security Engineer (cloud networking) and Generalist framing than SOC/VAPT entry listings.

scripting_programming.count_basis: Pentest/VAPT postings name Python most explicitly; SOC sources note it's increasingly expected but not always required at true Tier 1 (more Tier 2/3).

Genuinely dual-purpose — VAPT sources cite it for Windows AD exploitation, SOC/DFIR sources cite it for Windows incident investigation/automation — but weighted toward SOC because it surfaces more consistently in L1/L2 SOC skill lists than in generic VAPT tool lists where Metasploit/Burp dominate.
Linux-tooling-tied, tracks with the Kali Linux / Linux administration emphasis in VAPT postings.

soft_skills.count_basis: One of the most consistently tagged non-technical skills across this entire sample — undifferentiated by track.
VAPT sources specifically name clear findings/report writing as a defining output of the role (deliverable-driven pentest reports); SOC/NetSec need it but it's less the defining output.

Confirmed genuinely SOC-specific, not generic — explicitly and repeatedly called out for SOC roles at Indian IT services and MSSP firms specifically; essentially absent from VAPT, NetSec, or generalist/intern postings, which are typically standard-hours.
Named explicitly in both SOC (log triage precision) and VAPT (vulnerability identification precision) sources as a differentiator; less emphasized in Network Security Engineer postings.
